questions.prompt: Put the phases of a well-structured test in order.

items.text: Arrange — set up inputs and state
Act — perform the one action under test
Assert — compare the result to the expectation

questions.explanation: Arrange-Act-Assert is the standard shape: prepare, do the single action, then check the outcome.

options.text: Each test may contain exactly one assert statement, always
Each test targets one behavior, even if it takes a few related asserts
Each test file may contain only one test

questions.explanation: The rule is one behavior per test. Several assertions about the same behavior are fine; avoid mixing unrelated behaviors.

questions.prompt: Which test names are good because they describe behavior? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Good names state subject, condition, and expected result; test_1 and test_stuff communicate nothing in a failure report.

questions.prompt: AAA is a fold of Meszaros's Four-Phase Test: setup, exercise, verify, and ____ (handled by the framework in AAA).
questions.explanation: The Four-Phase Test adds teardown/cleanup, which AAA leaves to the framework's fixtures/cleanup.

questions.prompt: Why is a single test that checks four unrelated behaviors a problem?

options.text: It runs faster than four separate tests
The first failing assert stops the test, hiding the rest, and the name can't say what broke
pytest refuses to collect tests with multiple asserts
It improves the readability of the report

questions.explanation: Because assertions short-circuit on the first failure, a grab-bag test hides later problems and gives an ambiguous failure.

questions.prompt: Match each test phase or concept to what it does.

pairs.right: Prepare inputs and the world under test
Perform the single action being tested
Check the result against the expectation
Makes the report read like a spec

questions.explanation: Each phase has a distinct job; a descriptive name turns the verbose report into documentation.
